scenarios.title: Open the contact page and review the published support details
scenarios.intent: Prove the contact page presents the heading, support hours, and phone number an author needs before contacting support.
scenarios.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to separate the page's static support-details promise from its route-back-to-submissions promise. Negative, boundary, auth, and state-flow techniques were not applicable because the cited source specifies no input, failure mode, access gate, or multi-step state transition. Budget ceiling is 3 pairs; this scenario was kept because all 2 candidate scenarios fit within budget.

scenarios.title: Open the contact page and follow the submissions guidance link
scenarios.intent: Prove the contact page tells the reader to quote a SUB- reference number and routes them to `/my-submissions` for submission help.
scenarios.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to model the distinct outcome-changing navigation promise separately from the static contact-details display. Pagination, boundary value, negative, auth, and state-flow techniques were not applicable because the source names a single link target and no alternate outcomes or constrained inputs. Budget ceiling is 3 pairs; this scenario was kept because all 2 candidate scenarios fit within budget.

judgements.rationale: Happy-path coverage is applicable because the source explicitly promises the `/contact` heading, support hours, and phone number. Negative, boundary, security, perf, and i18n variants are not applicable because no source text specifies invalid inputs, limits, gated access, timing bound, or locale-variant output for this page.

A separate happy-path scenario is applicable because the source explicitly promises both guidance to quote a `SUB-` reference number and a link to `/my-submissions`, which creates a navigation outcome distinct from merely displaying support details.
